faqs.question: I am unable to connect my product to a wireless network. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The printer does not come with built-in wireless features and does not support a wireless (or Ethernet) connection to a network router. Only a direct wired connection to the computer is supported.

faqs.question: I can't scan multiple document pages into a single PDF. What should I do?
faqs.answer: If you are using the Scanner Driver and Epson Scan Utility v2.92a or earlier, the ability to scan multiple pages to a single PDF is not supported. This feature is supported when using the Scanner Driver (which is sometimes shown as TWAIN Driver) and Epson Scan Utility v3.04a or higher. Check your product's Downloads tab to make sure you're using the latest version.

faqs.question: Can the Epson ink cartridges be refilled or can I use third-party ink cartridges without voiding the warranty?
faqs.answer:
Epson does not recommend refilling or using other brands of ink cartridges.  Epson uses a permanent Micro Piezo print head that has allowed Epson to lead the industry in delivering consistent photo image quality by using variable-sized droplets.  Micro Piezo print head can also use a wider variety of inks, which has allowed Epson to introduce such ink breakthroughs as DURABrite® and Epson UltraChrome® inks that offer greatly improved humidity resistance, smudge resistance, and fade resistance.
Using refilled ink cartridges will not void the product's original warranty; however, if these products cause a failure, the repair of that failure will not be covered under warranty.

faqs.question: My product is out of color ink even though I print in black only. Why does this happen?
faqs.answer:
To keep the print head clear, the printer uses a small amount of ink from all the cartridges whenever it prints. Even if you select
Black Only
, some color ink is still being used.

Close programs that you're not using.
Increase your system's memory.

faqs.question: I see the message Scanner Not Ready or Epson Scan will not start in Windows or on my Mac. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Make sure your EPSON Stylus RX500 is turned on and securely connected to your computer or USB hub.
If it is connected to a USB hub, make sure it's connected to a first tier hub. The first tier hub is the hub closest to the host computer when more than one hub is connected to the computer.
Check to make sure the scanner's transportation lock is unlocked.
Make sure you turn on the EPSON Stylus RX500 before you turn on your computer.
Try restarting your computer.

faqs.question: What's the best way to resize images if I want to scan them and make them larger?
faqs.answer: If you plan to enlarge your image, it is better to enlarge it when you're scanning rather than in your application. Each time you modify an image, you lose some quality.  Keep in mind when you enlarge a small photo, such as a 35 mm slide or wallet-size photo, you'll need to scan at a high enough resolution to retain your image quality, but not so high that your file size is too large to be efficient.  You must manually adjust the resolution (dpi) to maintain the same image quality when you resize your image.

faqs.question: Does the type of paper I use really make a difference?
faqs.answer:
The ink in this printer works great on inexpensive uncoated paper for your everyday printing needs.
For high quality printouts and for long lasting images such as photos, it is important to use genuine EPSON paper. EPSON paper has been specifically developed to be compatible with the ink formula used in EPSON printers.
Other brands of paper may not be compatible with the EPSON dye-based inks. These papers may give you lower quality color images and may not have the longevity of EPSON's long lasting media. Also, the ink also may not dry properly, causing pages to stick together and smearing.

faqs.question: Can I use sheet labels with my product?

faqs.question: How do I decide which resolution to select when scanning from Epson Scan?
faqs.answer:
The best scanning resolution depends on the purpose of the scan.
If you are enlarging your image, you must increase the resolution (dpi) proportionally to maintain the resolution of your original.
Higher resolution settings result in larger file sizes. For example, an 8.5 x 11-inch original scanned at 300 dpi can produce a 24MB file. The same original scanned at 72 dpi creates only a 1.3MB file. Large files take longer to process and print, so consider the practical limitations of your computer system when selecting a resolution. To keep your file size manageable, select the lowest possible resolution that gives acceptable quality.

faqs.question: Should I use the Photo RPM setting on my product driver's Advanced menu for printing everyday photos?
faqs.answer: For most photos and other print tasks, EPSON recommends the default print settings for the paper type you have selected. By using the default print settings, you achieve both excellent image quality and faster print speeds. With Microsoft Windows, simply select the Quality Option (Text, Photo, etc.) and then the paper type (Matte Paper-Heavyweight, Glossy Photo Paper, etc). The printer driver will automatically set the appropriate print settings. Photo RPM is intended for those exceptional print jobs where image quality is the primary consideration.
